messages:
maya: heads-up — customer reported unpredictable routing: X-Region header present sometimes, but cache keys differ. suspect rewrite ordering bug.
ben: which route? can you paste an example request?
maya: GET /v1/predict?model=fast&debug=true
maya: platform rule set: global inject X-Region, tenant rule strips debug from query, and path normalization lowercases service id.
maya: hypothesis: path normalization runs before query strip, so ?debug ends up being kept in cache key for some routes.
samir: ah — we had that ordering flip in the new envoy filter PR. ordering is: 1) path normalize, 2) header injection, 3) query rewrite — but for caching we compose cache key after header injection which is inconsistent.
elaine: oof. that explains why some canary traffic saw stale responses.
ben: can we run a quick repro? maya, can you share the raw proxy logs for a hit and a miss?
maya: pasted logs to #incidents-private — short extracts here: 
```
RECEIVED: GET /V1/PREDICT?MODEL=fast&debug=true Host: api.redwood.dev X-Tenant: acme
AFTER_NORMALIZE: GET /v1/predict?MODEL=fast&debug=true
AFTER_HEADER_INJECT: X-Region: us-west-2
AFTER_QUERY_REWRITE: GET /v1/predict?MODEL=fast
CACHE_KEY_COMPUTED: /v1/predict?model=fast|X-Region=us-west-2
```
	
ben: so logs show query param normalized to lowercase but debug not stripped until after cache key computation in some code paths.
samir: yep. the bug is that cache key computation is triggered in the routing layer before the query-rewrite filter runs for regex-based rules. for prefix rules it's fine.
elaine: is this a policy ordering thing or a config bug in the plugin?
samir: policy ordering. we register filters in two places: static pipeline and dynamic tenant policies. dynamic ones were appended and not guaranteed to run before cache key generation.
maya: customer is on Dedicated — they saw it in canary with dedupe enabled. need hotfix?
ben: low risk hotfix: move query-rewrite filter earlier than cache-key hook. can we scope to just tenant policies to avoid broad behavior change?
elaine: agree. also add regression test for a case where header injection occurs but query param is removed pre-cache.
samir: I'll open PR with test and changelog note. tentative patch: flip order of filter execution for dynamic policies and add explicit hook to recompute cache-key after final rewrite. snippet:
```
# pseudo
apply_filters(request):
  normalize_path(request)
  inject_headers(request)   # keep
  rewrite_query_params(request)
  recompute_cache_key_if_mutated(request)
```

ben: +1 to recompute. that avoids surprises if future filters mutate request.
maya: console UX note: in Redwood Console, when you inspect a route, we should show effective rewrite order and computed cache key for a sample request. customers asked for that during support call.
elaine: great idea. add a small "effective pipeline" panel under route details. show precedence: RouteOverrides > TenantPolicies > GlobalDefaults > EnvoyStatic.
ben: also recommend showing when a cache key was recomputed and by which filter (trace id). helps debugging.
ops-bot: deploy queued: patch/route-rewrite-ordering -> staging (id: dr-879)
maya: thanks — can we run canary with dedupe off for the customer's route until patch lands? want to avoid live mismatch.
samir: done. I set dedupe=false for tenant acme, pushed policy.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded to staging in 35s — preview URL: https://staging.console.redwood.dev/patch/dr-879
ben: once PR merged, we should communicate in console release notes and send a short note to CS about the dedupe toggle and the reasoning.
elaine: also add a small telemetry metric: rewrite_mutation_count and cache_key_recompute_count, and an alert if recompute_count spikes > 0 for tenants with dedupe enabled.
maya: filing a follow-up ticket for console UX + telemetry.
samir: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5129 — includes unit + integration test and changelog.
maya: thanks all — keeping customer updated. :thumbsup:
